issues: [security][info][confidence:high] Site 1 fix (verb-loop gate now `"$__STRIPPED" != "$NORM_TOK"`) held against every command-substitution-only split shape tried: all 5 ARM_DELETE_VERBS_UNCONDITIONAL verbs, splits at multiple internal positions simultaneously (`r$(true)m$(true)dir .claude`, `un$(true)li$(true)n$(true)k .claude`), two/three splitting substitutions in one token, mixed $(...) and backtick splitters in the same token (`r$(true)`true`m -rf .claude`), and a splitter whose output is non-empty but irrelevant (`r$(echo x)m -rf .claude`). A splitter whose output happens to be a real verb fragment (`r$(printf rm)m -rf .claude`) is caught earlier by Layer 2's INDIRECT_PATTERNS regex (BLOCKED, stronger than ask) before it would even reach the token layer.

[security][info][confidence:high] Site 3 fix (fourth scan copy + __mask_opaque_spans reuse in __note_opaque_verb) held against nesting depths beyond what the 36th round's committed 15-cell sweep covers (which is 1-level $(...) only): 2-level (`f$(echo $(true))ind .claude -delete`), 3-level, and 4-level $(...)-in-$(...) nesting; $(...)-in-backtick and backtick-in-$(...) mixed delimiter nesting; a verb split by a nested substitution that itself contains a real backtick sub as its argument; the -delete predicate split by a nested substitution (previously undertested -- the 36th round's bats tests only lock in the verb split, not the predicate split, in the nested-span shape). All returned ask.

[security][medium][confidence:high] Found two payloads that the live hook returns allow for, which neither the 35th nor 36th verdict's evidence enumerates: (1) `` `r$(echo `true`)m -rf .claude` `` (a $(...) whose argument contains an unescaped inner backtick) and (2) `$(r$(true))m -rf .claude` (an outer $(...) wrapping a verb-splitting inner $(...) at the very start of the wrapped content). Both were reproduced directly against the hook (jq | ./hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh) as allow. HOWEVER, confirmed in an isolated lab with real bash eval that NEITHER is an actual security bypass: (1) is a real bash syntax error (nested backticks require backslash-escaping to nest; unescaped, the second backtick closes the first span early and bash rejects the resulting command with a parse error) -- nothing executes, .claude survives. (2) resolves at runtime to running the nonexistent command `m -rf .claude` (the outer $(...) captures stdout of running literal command `r` -- which fails, produces empty stdout -- so the final command is `m -rf .claude`, not `rm -rf .claude`; `m: command not found`, .claude survives). Both are guard/real-shell semantic mismatches (the guard's opaque-span parser is more permissive about what counts as a valid nested span than real bash's own grammar), not exploitable holes. Reporting per the task's instruction to flag anything found even without full certainty -- these do NOT change the security verdict since no actual deletion is achievable through either shape, but they are a slightly different flavor of gap than the class this file's 36 rounds have been chasing (predicting a shell PARSE outcome, not just a value), worth a note in criteria_gaps for a future round to decide whether to special-case (most likely not worth the complexity given zero real exploitability).

[security][info][confidence:high] Both of the file's own declared/accepted residuals -- `$(${Z:-r}${Z:-m} -rf .claude)` (operator-form parameter expansion) and `r$(echo m)m -rf .claude` variants (nested-substitution-output verb, undecidable from the string) -- were independently re-derived to still return allow post-fix, for the same documented reason (masking cannot know a substitution's runtime output), consistent with both the 15th verdict's original declaration and the 36th verdict's re-confirmation.

[code_quality][info][confidence:high] Re-traced __note_opaque_verb() end to end independently: confirmed no early return exists (single straight-line body, save at entry / restore at the last statement). Built the function's own call graph by grep, not by reading the 36th verdict's claim: it calls __scan_opaque_verb_matches() (reads SPLIT_TOKS/ARM_DELETE_VERBS_UNCONDITIONAL only, never touches __OPAQUE_END), __strip_dollar_brace() (writes only __STRIPPED, never __OPAQUE_END), and __mask_opaque_spans() (the only path that transitively reaches __skip_backtick()/__skip_dollar_paren(), the sole writers of __OPAQUE_END anywhere in the file per a fresh `grep -n __OPAQUE_END` over the whole file). No other function in the file writes __OPAQUE_END. Confirmed __OPAQUE_END is never read anywhere inside __note_opaque_verb()'s own body between the save and the restore -- the only internal consumer of a freshly-set __OPAQUE_END is __mask_opaque_spans()'s own loop cursor (`k=$__OPAQUE_END`), which consumes it for its own purposes in the same statement it was set, not as a stale read of the outer save. The only other consumer of __OPAQUE_END in the whole file besides __tokenize_segment() is __split_segments() (lines ~1740-1758) -- traced it independently and confirmed it calls __skip_backtick/__skip_dollar_paren directly and consumes __OPAQUE_END immediately, never calling __note_opaque_verb or __mask_opaque_spans, so it is structurally unable to hit this bug class.

[code_quality][info][confidence:high] Independently re-did the whole-file global-variable audit rather than trusting the 36th verdict's list. Grepped every bare (non-local) assignment in the file and additionally traced __scan_one_segment_for_cp_delete()'s own RECURSION (it calls itself at two sites, ~2456 and ~2494, for wrapper-unwrap re-scans -- this recursion was not called out by name in either the 35th or 36th verdict's global audit, though it is exactly the 'nested call' shape the task asked about). Confirmed it is safe: the recursive calls always pass try_unwrap=0, which structurally prevents the recursive invocation from ever reaching the code path that sets __SEG_TOKS/__UNWRAP_CANDIDATES/__PREFIX_STRIP_CANDIDATES/__PREFIX_STRIP_OVERFLOW/__FIND_WRAPPED_ARG_OVERFLOW (all gated behind `if [[ "$try_unwrap" -eq 1 ]]`), so none of those globals can be clobbered by the recursion before the outer frame is done reading them. NORM_TOK's own producer/consumer pair (normalize_path_token) is confined to the per-token loop that completes before recursion is ever reached in the same invocation. Also independently found that the codebase had already defended against this exact bug class once before, proactively: __control_plane_location_impl() (recursive brace-expansion resolver) takes explicit local copies of BRACE_PRE/BRACE_POST before recursing (`local pre="$BRACE_PRE" post="$BRACE_POST"`, line ~1316) with an inline comment naming precisely the failure mode this task asked to hunt for ('the recursion overwrites the global before the second item can use it'). This is corroborating evidence the pattern is understood as a recurring class in this file, not a one-off blind spot, but it is also exactly the kind of thing that could regress in a future edit if a maintainer removes the local copy without re-reading that comment -- flagging as a standing regression risk, not a currently-open bug.
